paper.title: An Optimal Algorithm for Bandit and Zero-Order Convex Optimization with Two-Point Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit convex optimization with two-point feedback (general domain / norm)
unmapped: Learner plays w_t in W and suffers f_t(w_t) but chooses two separate query points w_t +/- delta_t u_t (possibly slightly outside W) whose values are observed
settings.definition_quote: At each round $t$, the adversary picks a convex function $f_t$ on $\reals^d$, which is not revealed to the learner. The learner then chooses a point $\bw_t$ from some known and closed convex set $\Wcal\subseteq \reals^d$, and suffers a loss $f_t(\bw_t)$. As feedback, the learner may choose two points $\bw'_t,\bw''_t\in \Wcal$ and receive $f_t(\bw_t'),f_t(\bw_t'')$.

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit convex optimization with two-point feedback on the simplex (1-norm geometry)
unmapped: Losses are Lipschitz with respect to the 1-norm (constant G_1)
Query points may lie slightly outside W
settings.definition_quote: the domain $\Wcal$ is the simplex in $\reals^d$, $d>1$ ... Suppose $f_t$ for all $t$ is $G_1$-Lipschitz with respect to the $L_1$ norm.

algorithms.name: Two-Point Bandit Convex Optimization Algorithm (mirror descent with symmetric two-point gradient estimator)

symbols.p_dual: bound on (E||u||_*^4)^{1/4} for u uniform on the unit sphere, dual norm of the mirror-descent norm
symbols.R_reg: R with sup_{w in W} r(w) <= R^2, r the 1-strongly convex regularizer

conditions: f_t convex and L_lip-Lipschitz w.r.t. the 2-norm
r is 1-strongly convex w.r.t. a norm with sup_W r <= R_reg^2
f_t can be queried at w_t +/- delta_t u_t

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: If $\eta = \frac{R}{p_{*} G_2 \sqrt{dT}}$, and $\delta_t$ chosen such that $\delta_t\leq p_*R\sqrt{\frac{d}{T}}$, then the sequence $\bw_1,\ldots,\bw_T$ generated by the algorithm satisfies the following for any $T$ and $\bw^*\in\Wcal$: \E[\frac{1}{T}\sum f_t(\bw_t)-\frac{1}{T}\sum f_t(\bw^*)] \leq c~p_{*} G_2R\sqrt{\frac{d}{T}}

results.notes: Paper bounds average regret; multiplied by T. Regret is against fixed w* with expectation over the learner's randomness. G_2 mapped to L_lip. Proof gives constant (c+2).

symbols.R: radius of a Euclidean ball containing W

conditions: f_t convex and L_lip-Lipschitz w.r.t. the Euclidean norm
tuning: eta and delta_t as in Theorem 1 with p_* = 1

source.label: cor:2

results.notes: Average regret multiplied by T. Paper says it matches Duchi et al.'s lower bound up to constants. Also implies optimization error bound for zero-order stochastic optimization.

symbols.G_1: Lipschitz constant of f_t with respect to the 1-norm

conditions: W is the simplex in R^d
f_t convex and G_1-Lipschitz w.r.t. the 1-norm
tuning: 1-norm, entropic regularizer r(w) = sum_i w_i log(d w_i)
eta and delta_t as in Theorem 1

source.label: cor:1
source.quote: Suppose $f_t$ for all $t$ is $G_1$-Lipschitz with respect to the $L_1$ norm. Then using $\norm{\cdot}=\norm{\cdot}_1$ and $r(\bw)=\sum_{i=1}^{d}w_i\log(d w_i)$, it holds for some constant $c$ and any $\bw^*\in\Wcal$ that ... \leq c~G_1 \sqrt{\frac{d\log^2(d)}{T}}.

results.notes: Average regret multiplied by T. Algorithm needs G_1 (not in vocabulary) for tuning. Matches Duchi et al. lower bound up to log factor.

cited_results.cited_title: Optimal rates for zero-order optimization: the power of two function evaluations
cited_results.setting_description: Zero-order stochastic convex optimization with two function evaluations, G_2-Lipschitz convex functions over a Euclidean ball of radius R; optimization error (equivalently average regret)
